To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) neonicotinoidal insecticides are present in the particulate emitted by drilling machines during corn sowing, and (ii) the direct contamination of single honeybees by the emitted particulate may cause lethal effects.

(i) the environmental exposure of bees to particulate matter coming from corn coated with neonicotinoide insecticides can reach lethal levels and (ii) that this is a probable cause for the reported colony losses in the spring.

(a) the environmental exposure of bees to neonicotinoidal particles coming from the drilling machine is high enough to cause lethal intoxication and (b) the exposure level depends on the type of neonicotiniod insecticides used and on the type of the drilling machine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of the environmental exposure to and the intoxication of honeybees with the insecticides contained in particulate matter emitted by corn drilling machines.
a novel route of environmental exposure to neonicotinoidal insecticides, which has so far received little attention.
a possible underestimated route of exposure to neonicotinides, namely, the inhalation of particles coming from the corn seed coating, which can produce lethal intoxication effects for bees.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
seed-coated insecticides, when used in a sustainable way, do not represent a risk for bees.
the use of neonicotinid insecticides on corn seed coating is not sustainable and should be banned.

seed coating is not the only route of environmental contamination of bees with insecticides, but that the atmospheric emission of particles from drilling machines is an additional and underestimated route of contamination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the atmospheric emission of neonicotinid insecticides from corn seed coating is a relevant route of environmental contamination of bees and that the use of these insecticidal seed coatings should be carefully reconsidered.
the environmental release from corn seed-coated with neonicotininoids is a significant source of exposure to bees and that the environmental release is a cause of bee mortality.

the environmental release by the drilling machines of particulate matter, which contains the neonicotinoidal insecticide thiamethoxam, may represent a major route for the exposure of honeybee colonies to these insecticides, which is not considered in the risk assessment of the European Union.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the atmospheric emission of insecticided dust by drilling machines can produce direct intoxication of bees and that the environmental risk associated with this exposure route should be considered in the environmental risk assessment of seed-coated insecticides.
the environmental exposure of bees to the insecticides can be higher than expected, due to the emission of particles containing the insecticides.
seed-coated insecticides can be an underestimated source of environmental contamination and that the use of these insecticide seed treatments should be carefully evaluated.
